title: Ohio — waiting period before indemnity begins

Ohio: an injured worker who is unable to work serves a short waiting period before temporary total disability benefits begin to accrue. If the disability continues past a longer qualifying period, the waiting days are paid retroactively. Handlers should confirm the current waiting and retroactive thresholds against the state board's published schedule before quoting a first-payment date to a claimant.

Occupational disease claims run from a different trigger — usually diagnosis or last exposure — so a claim that looks time-barred on its date of injury may not be.

Surgical pre-authorisation disputes are resolved through the state's utilisation review process.

The two are alternatives, and which one produces the larger exposure drives the reserve on a claim with a permanent restriction.

A file whose date of injury is old is therefore not automatically time-barred, and the distinction is worth recording on the claim rather than re-derived each time it is questioned.
